sources.note: Catalogue lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List entries; no language descriptions, texts or lexical resources exist in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Eyoh, Julius A. & Robert Hedinger. 2008. Mfumte Orthography Guide. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not Viti, but the nearest documented Nkambe-cluster lect to the Antere lects (Fum/Mfumte, Ncha/Ndaktup, Kwak named alongside Viti); would show whether the cluster is described as purely tonal. Context only; cannot stand in for Viti (glottocode mfum1238).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Viti language' and 'Mfumte language' (wikitext via API, Sept 2026).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Viti stub cites only Ethnologue; no phonology. Mfumte page (neighbouring Nkambe cluster named at Antere) has an alphabet from Eyoh & Hedinger 2008, nothing on stress, and is a different language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. Overview of Bantoid. Afrika und Übersee 97.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No mention of Viti at all.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: the Atlas has NO entry for Viti/Vötö (V-entries run Vono, Vori, Voro, Vute, Vwezhi; the Grassfields index lists only Dzodinka, Lam Nso, Limbum, Yamba); Antere is mentioned only under entry 483 Yamba.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry Viti [vit] (Internet Archive copy 2016-03-06).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives only: alternate name Vötö; Taraba State, Sardauna LGA, Antere; status 6a; Narrow Grassfields, Unclassified. No typology field.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. [c. 2012-2015]. The Bantoid languages: a monograph (draft, 51 pp; rogerblench.info via the Internet Archive 2015).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Viti; the Nkambe-cluster section (Tables 21-22: Dzodinka, Kwaja, Mfumte, Ndaktup/Ncha', Mbe', Limbum, Yamba) does not mention Viti. Classification and lexical isoglosses only.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Bruce Connell. 1999. A preliminary report of linguistic fieldwork undertaken in Jan 1999 (Mambila Plateau field trip). Web report, Virtual Institute of Mambila Studies (mambila.info/).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lists the five lects reported at Antere (Fum, Nshi, Kwak, Anca, and 'Bɨtɨ people speaking (?) Nde gbite' = Viti); says only a wordlist of the last was obtained and it is 'definitely a Grassfields language'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1999. Field trip to record the status of some little-known Nigerian languages. Ogmios (Newsletter of the Foundation for Endangered Languages) 11: 11-14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.13: 'We were able to record a wordlist of Viti and it is definitely a Grassfields language of Camerounian Bantu type - but of what type and whether it is new cannot yet be known.' Survey note only; no phonological data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid records viti1241 (Viti) and ndeg1238 (Nde-Gbite, bookkeeping/spurious).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: zero descriptive references; Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less. Nde-Gbite comment confirms the same Blench 1999 report is the only source and 'no data for Nde-Gbite was ever recorded'.
